title.narrative: Strengthening communities' livelihoods and food security post-COVID-19 in Piaui

description.narrative:
This project seeks to support two groups of families who have been adversely affected by the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic in Piaui, north-eastern Brazil: 1) 250 families in a situation of food insecurity; and 2) 200 farming families who need support to commercialise their agricultural production post-pandemic. Caritas intends to link up the farming families with those living in food insecurity, by providing them with 3 food basket distributions made up of at least 33% agroecological family farmed produce. It will also provide BRL 3,500 (£552 @6.3) micro-credit to the farming families to support them to invest in their family-based farming and provide logistical support and equipment to access local markets.
Brazil was one of the hardest hit countries in the world by the COVID-19 pandemic: over 670,000 people died, and the knock-on socio-economic impacts led to it being put back on the World Food Programme’s World Hunger Map in 2020 (Brazil was removed in 2014 after a decade of progress in reducing hunger). But less than seven years later, more than half its 212 million population is grappling with some level of food insecurity – and almost one in 10 with serious hunger. The state of Piaui was heavily affected by the COVID-19 pandemic during multiple lockdowns where community-based markets and fairs were closed for long periods. The weakening of the livelihoods of local communities, based mainly on agricultural production and commercialisation, led to deepening inequalities and increasing food insecurity - Piauí was the Northeastern state with the highest increase in poverty rates between 2019 and 2021.
